title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context: this is the second draft of Grothendieck's 'Analysis situs' notes (1986), an attempt to axiomatize a 'tame' geometry of figures, in the spirit of the tame-topology programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5. The previous page recalls the set-up. M is a poset (morally the 'pieces' of a space, e.g. closed simplices or strata). It carries a family 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(M) of 'figures', which are subsets closed for the order (lower sets). The axioms are: 𝓕 contains every principal lower set M_{≤x} and the empty set; and 𝓕 satisfies a 'compatibility' (gluing) condition: if every M_{≤x} ∪ M_{≤y} with x∈F, y∈G lies in 𝓕, then F∪G∈𝓕. Conversely, (𝓕,⊆) with the conditions C1–C3 of GF IV (the 'first draft') recovers (M,≤): M_{≤x} is the smallest figure containing x, and points are separated by figures. On this page Grothendieck says he will not return to that equivalence. He announces the next topic: interpreting the formalism in terms of 'ombres' ('shadows', large or small). These are presumably the neighbourhood-type objects, open stars or regular neighbourhoods, from which opens are later built via a relation ≪. He fixes a methodological constraint. First he will treat only the 'algebraic' or 'trivial' aspects of the formalism of figures, and isolate the right arguments. These arguments must be valid (1°) in the purely set-theoretic model Fig(L): figures in a given set L, under some finiteness condition. They must also be valid (2°) for finite affine simplicial figures (polyhedra) in an affine space over ℝ, or more generally over an arbitrary ordered field. He then begins to describe the figures in terms of (M,≤). Definition (1.34): a figure F∈𝓕 is 'of finite type' iff its associated lower set F̃ is a finite union of principal lower sets M_{≤x_i}, for a finite family (x_i) in M; that is, F̃ is a finitely generated lower set. The next page shows the purpose. Under the finite-type hypothesis, 𝓕 is equivalent to a symmetric relation on M (written ≬, read as intersection or disjointness) that is stable under passing to smaller elements (1.36). So a 'space of figures' is morally (M, ≤, ≬). This then prepares the construction of opens via ≪, starting with the 'large opens'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; (1.34) is a definition. The notation F̃ is not defined on this page. It presumably denotes the lower set (saturation) in M attached to F, and the dual role of F (subset of M vs element of 𝓕) is ambiguous in the draft.

On the next page the relation ≬ is called 'réflexive' while being stable under passing to smaller elements. Read as an intersection relation this is plausible, but X ≬ X fails for an empty element, so the setting is slightly loose.

ideas.what: Requirement that the formalism of figures and its proofs work both for set-theoretic figures Fig(L) and for finite affine simplicial figures over an arbitrary ordered field (not just ℝ)
ideas.modern_name: Model-independent tame geometry; semilinear / o-minimal geometry over arbitrary (real closed or ordered) fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); semilinear sets: classical; van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures' (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, 'structures modérées') in spirit; the specific dual test models are not published

ideas.what: Figures of finite type = finitely generated lower sets of the poset M of pieces
ideas.modern_name: Finitely generated down-sets / compact elements in the lattice of lower sets (Alexandrov topology); finite subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Order theory / Alexandrov (1937); face posets of polyhedra

ideas.what: Plan to reinterpret the figure formalism via 'ombres' (large/small shadows), leading to opens via a relation ≪
ideas.modern_name: Open stars / regular neighbourhoods; way-below-like relation generating opens (cf. proximity spaces, continuous lattices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Regular neighbourhoods: Whitehead; way-below relation: Scott (1972); proximity: Efremovich

missed.claim: An axiomatic, essentially combinatorial foundation of tame topology: a poset of pieces M with closed 'figures', plus an intersection relation and a relation ≪ producing opens. It is designed so that the same 'trivial' arguments apply to abstract set figures and to semilinear polyhedra over any ordered field. This programme was never developed in the literature, where o-minimality took a model-theoretic route instead.
missed.quote: de telle façon que 1°) Ceux-ci soient valables dans tout ... Fig(L) ... et 2°) ... aux figures simpliciales affines finies, dans un espace affine sur ℝ (ou, plus généralement, sur un corps ordonné quelconque)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a non-model-theoretic, order-theoretic axiomatization of tame spaces. This could connect o-minimal / semilinear geometry with poset and Alexandrov-space methods (e.g. exit-path categories, face posets, combinatorial stratifications).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly programmatic. The finite-type definition is routine. The notable point is the explicit methodological double test (abstract set figures vs semilinear figures over arbitrary ordered fields) within an unpublished axiomatics of tame topology, together with the announced 'ombres' interpretation. This is mildly interesting historically but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 6 is probably 'et au souci de dégager les bons raisonnements' rather than 'et aux contraintes de cohérence [?] que les bons raisonnements'.
'Ceux-ci devraient [?] s'établir dans tout "abstrait"' is probably 'Ceux-ci soient valables dans tout "cadre"/"atelier" [?]'; similarly '2°) qu'ils soient valables aussi, disons, ...'.
Final parenthesis probably reads '(pour une suite [famille] finie d'éléments de M)'; the subscript is M_{≤x_i}.
